requirement:
Model tool descriptions SHOULD NOT explain cases the model meets only
occasionally, such as access policy, excluded or build-output paths, redaction,
paging, and failures, and the harness SHOULD explain each of these where it
occurs: in the tool error, or in a note in the result it affects. The model reads
every description on every assessment, so explaining rare cases there costs
attention on every review for a case most never meet, and access-policy wording
in particular can steer its reasoning away from the review. A tool whose purpose
is one of these cases, such as `next_page`, explains it in its description.
rationale:
The tests cover both halves of `requirements.authoring.tool_descriptions.special_cases`. The first half is that descriptions leave rare cases out. The second is that the harness explains each rare case where it occurs.

**Descriptions SHOULD NOT explain rare cases.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[descriptions_leave_paging_policy_redaction_and_failures_to_results]` lowercases every tool definition's description and asserts that none contains a marker for access policy, excluded or build-output paths, redaction, paging, or failures. The markers include "kib", "returned in pages", "redact", "credential", "denied", "disallow", "habeas.toml", "aborts", "untracked", "build output", "outside the project", "tool error", "policy", "ignore rules", "exclusion" and "permitted".
- The same test asserts that `next_page` takes only a `token` parameter.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[descriptions_give_each_argument_and_the_result_form]` covers the exception for a tool whose purpose is one of these cases. It asserts that `next_page`'s description explains its own purpose, using phrases such as "following page", "same shape" and "token is the page's next value".

**The harness SHOULD explain each case where it occurs.**
- **Access policy and untracked files.** `fn[untracked_diagnostics_name_git_add_and_an_allow_rule]` asserts that the tool error from `habeas` and `list_files` names `git add`, the `habeas.toml allow rule` and the path. It also asserts that the harness does not stage files or create `habeas.toml`.
- **Excluded evidence paths.** `fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]` asserts that reads, `list_files`, `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` on generated evidence return an error naming the path and "generated evidence". It covers `./` paths and symlinks. It also checks that discovery results leave the excluded paths out.
- **Build-output paths.** `fn[requests_for_book_or_target_output_are_ordinary_read_failures]` asserts that every tool, for both the default book directory and a configured `build-dir`, returns an error saying the path "holds build output" and that the sources are elsewhere in the project. It also checks that `book` is an ordinary directory when `build-dir` is set.
- **Out-of-project and recoverable errors.** `fn[unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors]` asserts the "outside the project" message. In `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]`, `fn[a_read_through_a_symlink_leaving_the_project_returns_an_error_to_the_model]` and `fn[malformed_and_failed_reads_return_to_the_model_and_the_assessment_continues]` assert that the error reaches the model in the next request.
- **Failures.** The malformed-read test covers malformed arguments, missing files, absent items and out-of-range lines. It asserts the failure text appears in the second provider request and not the first, and that the failed reads are not recorded.
- **Redaction.** `fn[only_results_with_redacted_text_carry_the_redaction_note]` asserts the note on `habeas` and `ripgrep` results that have redacted text. It asserts no note on results without redaction, including source or requirement text that merely contains the marker string.
- **Paging.** The test marked for `special_cases` is `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order]`. It calls the helper `all_pages`, which asserts that every page with a next token carries `page.note == PAGE_NOTE` ("call next_page with this page's next token") and that the last page has no note. `PAGE_NOTE` in `src/authoring/pages.rs` is itself marked as implementing this requirement. `fn[redacted_results_reserve_space_for_the_note_on_every_delivered_page]` repeats the paging-note assertion, but it is not marked for this requirement.
- **Glob handling.** `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[evidence_rules_are_literal_paths_not_globs]` checks that the `habeas.toml` rule is applied literally and that its denial message names the rule.

The keyword list in the description test is a heuristic. It still covers each category the requirement names. I found no unmarked relevant test and no obligation left unasserted, so I report no gap.
